title: Hierarchical stop-sequence resolver fix for customer eval noise
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A customer reported systematic noise and occasional overgeneration in their evaluation harness after a runtime change that harmonized sampling defaults across deployments. The symptom set differed by deployment mode: Hosted saw extraneous trailing phrases; Dedicated customers saw occasional truncation when they supplied 'hint_stop' sequences in request metadata; Private deployments produced inconsistent eval diffs compared to the customer's local baseline.

Root cause hypothesis and discovery:
- The serving stack has three logical sources of stop/termination sequences: 1) request-level customer hints (hint_stop), 2) model manifest stop sequences, and 3) runtime defaults. A change to the sampling defaults refactor inadvertently changed how stop sets were merged between the routing layer and the per-replica runtime.
- Specifically, when a request was routed to a fallback model variant (common in Dedicated autoscale and Private capacity handoffs), the routing layer serialized stop sequences as a merged set but failed to preserve explicit ordering and origin tags. The runtime resolver then applied a last-writer-wins merge instead of honoring request-level precedence, which caused (a) request hints to be dropped in favor of model defaults and (b) duplicate/overlapping sequences to be treated as distinct tokens resulting in partial matches that didn't trigger termination.
- We also observed inconsistent Unicode normalization between the router and runtime which caused stop-seq equality checks to fail for sequences containing non-ASCII punctuation used by a small set of customers.

Reproduction steps:
1) Use customer-supplied prompt and hint_stop set (attached test vector).
2) Route request to fallback model variant (simulate Dedicated burst routing or private pool node mismatch).
3) Compare streamed tokens between the pre-refactor baseline and the refactored runtime: extra tokens appear when request hint is not applied or when overlapping stop seqs fail to match.

Mitigation and fix implemented:
- Implemented a hierarchical stop-sequence resolver in the routing layer and runtime with explicit precedence: request.hint_stop > customer.profile > model.manifest > runtime.default. The resolver preserves ordering and origin metadata through the RPC layer.
- Added Unicode NFC normalization to all stop sequences at request ingest time and canonical deduplication logic that treats substring overlaps as single termination candidates (prefer longer match).
- Fixed the serialization contract between router and replica: stop sequences now transmit as (canonical_string, origin_tag) tuples and the runtime honors origin_tag precedence rather than last-write semantics.
- Quick patch (hotfix) rolled to Hosted within 24h to address high-impact customers; Dedicated and Private received staggered canary rollouts with strict rollback conditions (regression > 0.2 BLEU-like metric or any customer-eval failure).

Testing and validation:
- Added unit tests for the resolver covering precedence, overlap, and normalization cases.
- Added an e2e regression test that replays the customer evaluation harness on canary nodes and computes token-diff metrics against baseline.
- Instrumented Console with a temporary per-request flag (debug.stopseq_diff) to collect failing samples for customers during the canary window.

Rollout notes and monitoring:
- Hosted: hotfix deployed 2025-02-15 03:10 UTC, canary for 6 hours, full rollout by 2025-02-15 11:45 UTC.
- Dedicated: canary pool applied 2025-02-18; observed two minor diffs (investigated, unrelated sampling RNG seed mismatch fixed by ENG-61200). Full rollout 2025-02-25.
- Private: customers with active incidents (N=3) received private patches and assisted upgrade packages; one customer requested delayed patch (compliance window) and accepted mitigations.

Follow-ups and action items:
- PM to coordinate customer communications and confirm resolution of their eval suites (ACME Legal, DataSynth Inc.).
- Add a long-term linting job in CI that checks for stop-seq serialization contract changes. (ENG-61990 planned)
- Add telemetry to Dashboard: percent of requests where request.hint_stop was present and percent honored by runtime to detect future regressions.

Notes on why this is different from previous stop-related regressions:
This regression was caused by loss of precedence metadata during merge/serialization between routing and runtime (not by a single stop token ordering bug or tokenization mismatch alone). The fix required preserving origin metadata across RPC boundaries and introducing canonicalization/deduplication heuristics to handle overlapping sequences introduced by customer hints.

resolution: Implemented hierarchical resolver with preserved origin metadata, added NFC normalization and overlap deduplication, added unit and e2e regression tests, performed staggered canary rollouts across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and instrumented monitoring. Customer evals confirmed resolved.
postmortem_summary: Root cause: loss of origin metadata and improper merge semantics across router->runtime boundary after sampling-defaults refactor. Preventative: contract tests for stop-seq serialization, nightly regression harness inclusion, and telemetry for stop-seq honor rate.
notes: Third-party customers were anonymized in public artifacts. Related follow-up: ENG-61990 (lint CI) and ENG-62011 (dashboard telemetry retention increase).
